idiom_name: logic in lib.rs + thin main.rs (cargo test, traits or generics as seams)
implementation_notes: The Rust book prescribes this split directly: because main cannot be tested, move the program's logic into lib.rs, leave main.rs to read arguments, call a run function and map the error, and test the library with #[cfg(test)] mod tests under cargo test. What replaces the humble class is the library crate plus a trait or generic parameter for outbound collaborators, so a test can substitute a double without a mocking framework (mockall generates them when the trait grows). Keep the single-crate shape when the binary must stay small, accepting that its glue is then covered only by integration tests in tests/.
pitfalls: Private items are invisible to integration tests in tests/, which link the crate like any user; expose what you test, and keep unit tests inside the module for internal seams.
Generics versus dyn: a generic collaborator monomorphises and keeps tests fast, but a double that must be stored in a struct needs a trait object or an enum; decide per seam, not per project.
The shell's error mapping is only exercised through the process boundary (exit code, stderr), so it stays covered by one or two integration tests rather than by unit tests.
